note: Work: the Labour Code (Ley 185 of 1996), article 131 as replaced by Ley 474 (La Gaceta No. 199 of 21 October 2003): the minimum age to work for pay is 14, and work below it is prohibited; adolescents may sign employment contracts themselves from sixteen. The text makes no exception for performers, so the form holds them barred below 14 (my reading). Later reforms of article 131 weren't checked. Read from the Enrique Bolaños Foundation's digital copy of La Gaceta (the National Assembly's legislation site refused this client with 403). Majority: the Family Code (Ley 870, approved 24 June 2014, La Gaceta No. 190 of 8 October 2014), art. 21(a): full capacity to acquire rights, contract obligations and dispose of one's person and goods at eighteen; read 2026-11-03 in ecoi.net's copy of the Code as published (the National Assembly's site refused this client with 403). Emancipation by marriage, by a court or a parent's authorisation, and a parent of sixteen or seventeen having full capacity (art. 21(b), (c)) aren't held. Service: null. The State's initial report to the UN Committee on the Rights of the Child (CRC/C/OPAC/NIC/1, 4 March 2010, read 2026-11-03) says the 1995 constitutional reform did away with compulsory military service and forbids forced recruitment; the constitution was reformed again in 2025 and its current text wasn't read, so service isn't held (the game doesn't read it).
